title: Run Compare: inspect two real Measure snapshots
description: Compare two preserved real Measure outputs, inspect equal settings and counts, and distinguish missing results from a negative scientific finding.
objectives: Open Run Compare from the Home Data section and prepare the downloadable real-snapshot example.
Compare distinct historical runs without changing their recorded versions or settings.
Read settings, object counts and missing-result warnings without overstating the evidence.
prerequisite: Use Run_Compare_real_snapshots.zip and its README. In a spaCR environment run the included prepare_run_compare_download.py with a NEW destination folder, then Browse to that folder. This explicit helper transports only two selected, unchanged measurements databases and their historical artifact rows; it is not a GUI importer, new analysis or full project archive. The original full SHA-256 fingerprints match. Only project/path and a relocation note change: run IDs, artifact IDs, settings, versions and timestamps are retained. Runs d86c136e7261 and caa0bf7ca2ce were actually produced by spaCR 1.5.0.5 on 2026-09-11 at 03:37:56 and 04:05:56 UTC. Both contain 601 cells, 622 nuclei, 373 pathogen objects, 601 cytoplasm objects and 601 png_list rows across one plate, four wells and sixteen fields; all object identities match. Recorded settings are equal. Database hashes differ; no full-feature equality, segmentation accuracy, improved model or biological significance is claimed. No regression result is included. API: spacr.run_compare.runs_in and compare_runs with spacr.artifacts.Registry. No GPU, AI provider or new analysis is used. Original data are unchanged; nothing is published.

scenes.narration: Open Home, choose Data, then Run Compare. This is a main module, not a tool nested inside Regression. It reads recorded outputs from two runs. Our example uses two real Measure snapshots from the downloaded-data workflow; it does not invent a change just to make the comparison look interesting.

Download and extract the companion snapshot archive. In your spaCR environment, run its preparation script with a new destination folder, following the included readme. This explicitly relocates two unchanged databases and their historical records. It is not an automatic import button, a new analysis, or a complete copy of either original project.

Click Browse and select the prepared comparison folder. The helper preserves the original run identifiers, settings, versions, times and content hashes. Only the copied index's addresses and relocation note change. Keep original projects untouched; a historical run entry pointing at a database that has since been overwritten is not a preserved snapshot.

Choose the earlier Measure run as baseline A and the later run as B, then Compare. Both were produced by spaCR version one point five point zero point five. A newer viewer does not change that history. Here settings and counts match; this is a consistency demonstration, not evidence that a model improved.

Enable Show unchanged settings to inspect the recorded values. The zero on the Settings tab means no differences, not that no settings were saved. Expand the entries and compare the values themselves. These two runs used identical recorded settings; this example therefore cannot show the effect of changing a parameter.

Counts shows six hundred one cells and six hundred twenty-two nuclei in each run, across sixteen fields and four wells. Delta is B minus A; every displayed delta is zero. The independent check also matched object identities. Equal totals alone would not prove that the same objects or all measured feature values were identical.

Hits says no regression results were registered. These snapshots contain measurements only, so there is no ranked hit comparison to display. This does not mean that a regression found no significant hits: no regression result is present here. Use the Regression and Run History tutorials to trace the required outputs.

Selecting the same run on both sides produces a warning. Read it rather than treating a comparison result as automatic validation. Return to two distinct runs and check their source, version and scope before drawing conclusions. A warning is a reason to investigate, not an instruction to force a result.

The distinct pair is restored, and the original files remain unchanged. Run Compare is a read-and-compare workflow; it does not rerun Measure or need a GPU or AI provider. Python exposes runs_in and compare_runs for the same comparison. Preserve actual output snapshots and document their provenance before comparing your own runs.
